night-sky.text: Night falls: clear the window to a night sky – almost black, perhaps with a hint of blue.

hint.opengl: It is the clear colour of the render loop: `glClearColor`. Something like (0.02, 0.02, 0.08) – every channel well below the old teal.
hint.vulkan: It is the clear value of the colour attachment in `recordCommandBuffer()`: `clearValues[0].color`. Something like (0.02, 0.02, 0.08).
hint.d3d12: It is the `clearColor` array that `PopulateCommandList` hands `ClearRenderTargetView`. Something like (0.02, 0.02, 0.08).

observatory.text: A seat in the gallery: start the camera above and behind the middle of the world, looking down at it from an angle – for example 6 units up and 8 back – and keep the free camera working.

hint.opengl: Change the globals: `cameraPos` (0, 6, 8) and `cameraFront` pointing back at the origin, (0, -0.6, -0.8). Start `pitch` at about -36.87° (its sine is -0.6), so the first mouse movement doesn't make the view jump.
hint.vulkan: Change the globals: `cameraPos` (0, 6, 8) and `cameraFront` pointing back at the origin, (0, -0.6, -0.8). Start `pitch` at about -36.87° (its sine is -0.6), so the first mouse movement doesn't make the view jump.
hint.d3d12: Change the global `XMVECTOR`s: `cameraPos` (0, 6, 8) and `cameraFront` pointing back at the origin, (0, -0.6, -0.8). Start `pitch` at about -36.87° (its sine is -0.6), so the first mouse movement doesn't make the view jump.

sun.text: Let there be a sun: instead of the ten crates, draw one crate in the middle of the world, about twice as big, slowly turning around its own vertical (y) axis.

hint.opengl: Replace the `for` loop with one draw. Its model matrix: `glm::rotate` by the time around (0, 1, 0), then `glm::scale` by 2 – no translation, the sun stays at the origin. The cube positions are not needed any more.
hint.vulkan: Replace the `for` loop in `recordCommandBuffer()` with one push and one draw. The model matrix: `glm::rotate` by `glfwGetTime()` around (0, 1, 0), then `glm::scale` by 2 – no translation, the sun stays at the origin.
hint.d3d12: Replace the `for` loop in `PopulateCommandList` with one draw. The model matrix: `XMMatrixScaling(2.0f, 2.0f, 2.0f) * XMMatrixRotationY(…)` with the time – no translation, the sun stays at the origin.

planet.text: A planet: a second, smaller crate that circles the sun at a fixed distance, a few units out.

hint.opengl: Keep the orbit in a matrix of its own: `rotate` by the time around (0, 1, 0), then `translate` out along x. Read from the bottom up: first moved out, then turned around the sun. Scale a copy of it for the draw.
hint.vulkan: Keep the orbit in a matrix of its own: `rotate` by the time around (0, 1, 0), then `translate` out along x. Read from the bottom up: first moved out, then turned around the sun. Scale a copy of it, push it and draw.
hint.d3d12: Keep the orbit in a matrix of its own: `XMMatrixTranslation(3.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f) * XMMatrixRotationY(…)` – first moved out, then turned around the sun. The planet's model matrix is a scaling times that.

moon.text: A moon: a third, even smaller crate that circles the planet while the planet circles the sun.

hint.opengl: Start the moon's matrix from the planet's orbit matrix (before its scale): `glm::rotate(planet, …)` faster, then `translate` a little way out, then a small `scale`.
hint.vulkan: Start the moon's matrix from the planet's orbit matrix (before its scale): `glm::rotate(planet, …)` faster, then `translate` a little way out, then a small `scale`.
hint.d3d12: End the moon's chain with the planet's orbit matrix (before its scale): scaling, then a short translation, then a faster rotation around y, then `* planet`.

text.opengl: Colour: give every body its own colour – a uniform in `shader.fs`, set before each draw – and mix it with the crate's texture so the wood still shows.
text.vulkan: Colour: give every body its own colour – after the model matrix in the push constants, read by the fragment shader – and mix it with the crate's texture so the wood still shows.
text.d3d12: Colour: give every body its own colour – after the model matrix in the root constants, read by the pixel shader – and blend it with the crate's texture so the wood still shows.

hint.opengl: `uniform vec3 bodyColor;` in `shader.fs`, `FragColor = mix(texColor, vec4(bodyColor, 1.0), 0.6);`, and `ourShader.setVec3("bodyColor", …)` before each `glDrawArrays`.
hint.vulkan: Add `vec3 color` to the push constant block in both shaders and `glm::vec3 color` to the C++ struct; the range and every `vkCmdPushConstants` need `VK_SHADER_STAGE_VERTEX_BIT | VK_SHADER_STAGE_FRAGMENT_BIT`.
hint.d3d12: Add `float3 color` to `cbuffer ModelConstants` and `XMFLOAT3 color` to the C++ struct; make the root constants visible to every stage (`D3D12_SHADER_VISIBILITY_ALL`) and `lerp` in `PSMain`.
